headline: Presidential election vote today after 35 years, with two candidates contesting
summary: Bangladesh's presidential election will be held today with 349 MPs casting votes. BNP's Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is expected to win against Oli Ahmad of the 11-party alliance, marking the first contested presidential poll in 35 years.
details: Bangladesh is holding its presidential election today, marking the first time in 35 years that the top office will be decided by a vote. The election features two candidates: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir from the ruling BNP and Oli Ahmad representing an 11-party alliance. Voting will take place in the Jatiya Sangsad from 2 PM to 5 PM.

A total of 349 Members of Parliament (MPs) are eligible to cast their votes. Despite the presence of two candidates, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir's victory is virtually assured due to the BNP's overwhelming majority with 247 members in Parliament. The electoral schedule mandates a vote because there are multiple candidates.

This election marks only the second time MPs will vote for a president since the reintroduction of the parliamentary system in 1991. The seven subsequent presidents were all elected unopposed, making today's contest a significant event in the nation's democratic process.

The presidential election vote is not secret; MPs will write their preferred candidate's full name and sign on the ballot paper. The Chief Whip has announced that the newly elected president will take the oath of office tomorrow, Friday, at 7 PM at Bangabhaban.

The presidential post became vacant following the resignation of Md. Shahabuddin, who was elected during the Awami League's tenure, on July 24. The Election Commission (EC) announced the election schedule on August 6, fulfilling the constitutional requirement to elect a new president within 90 days of the vacancy.

Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) A.M.M. Nasir Uddin is serving as the electoral officer for this election. As the Parliament is not currently in session, a separate meeting of MPs has been convened specifically for the voting process, which the CEC will preside over and manage.

MPs will cast their votes from their respective seats. They will first receive a ballot paper, signing their full name on the counterfoil, and then sign again on the main ballot next to their chosen candidate's name. The current Speaker, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, and Acting Speaker, Kaiser Kamal, are also eligible to vote as MPs.

BNP candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, being an MP, is entitled to vote for himself. His parliamentary seat will become vacant on the day he assumes the presidential office. Conversely, Oli Ahmad is not an MP and therefore cannot participate in the voting process.

CEC A.M.M. Nasir Uddin informed journalists yesterday that the voting by the Speaker and the Prime Minister would be broadcast live on BTV at the beginning of the process, after which the broadcast would pause. Live coverage will resume during the vote counting, and the results will be announced in the Parliament chamber by the electoral officer upon completion of counting, followed by a gazette notification.

The Jatiya Sangsad has a total of 350 seats, including 50 reserved for women. However, due to a court order regarding the Chittagong-4 constituency, the result for that seat has not yet been declared, bringing the current number of MPs and presidential electors to 349.

The ruling BNP holds 247 parliamentary seats. They are supported by one MP each from allied parties: Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP), Gono Odhikar Parishad, and Gono Sanghati Andolon. The Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance commands 90 MPs, including 77 from Jamaat-e-Islami and one woman MP elected with Jamaat's support.

Additionally, the alliance includes eight members from the Jatiya Nagorik Party (NCP), three from Bangladesh Khelafat Majlish, and one from Khelafat Majlish. There is also one MP from Islami Andolon Bangladesh and eight independent members.

The BNP has reportedly sought votes from the independent MPs. Sources indicate that the Islami Andolon MP may abstain from voting. This complex political landscape underscores the significance of each vote in the contested election.

The last contested presidential election in 1991 saw BNP's Abdur Rahman Biswas win with 172 votes against Awami League's Justice Badrul Haider Chowdhury, who secured 92 votes. At that time, no party achieved a single majority, and BNP formed the government with the support of Jamaat-e-Islami.

headline: Nine killed, six Bangladeshis among victims in Kolkata hotel fire
summary: A devastating fire at a Kolkata hotel claimed nine lives, including six Bangladeshi nationals. Among the deceased are a journalist's family of four from Kushtia, two from Satkhira, and one from Savar.
details: Nine people, including six Bangladeshi citizens, were killed in a hotel fire in Kolkata, India, early Wednesday morning. The blaze, which started around 2 AM on Tuesday night, also injured several others.

Among the Bangladeshi victims were journalist Debashish Dutta (39) from Kushtia, his wife Afsana Sharmin (27), their three-year-old son Swarnashish Dutta, and Debashish's father-in-law Akram Ali (64). This family of four perished together.

Two residents of Kaligonj Upazila in Satkhira, Alimuzzaman Saju (45) and Rebati Sarkar, were also identified among the deceased. Saju, a ghair businessman, had traveled to India for medical treatment.
Another Bangladeshi victim was Ahmed Babu (40) from Aminbazar, Savar, Dhaka. The hotel reportedly housed 25 Bangladeshi nationals at the time of the incident.

The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata promptly dispatched officials to the site to gather information on the deceased and injured. Satkhira district police are also investigating the details of the incident.
